Can not reproduce issue.

`Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Single-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated Intel(R) HD Graphics 620 (Intel Corporation; 31.0.101.2115) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-7130U CPU @ 2.70GHz (4 threads) - 7.86 GiB memory`

Interestingly I was able to reproduce the issue in any form from your steps to reproduce, but not by using your MRP, only a fresh project or a long term project of mine has this issue. This issue is preventing me from working on my project on that area, I'm going to have to wait until it is addressed hopefully soon.

`Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Single-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4790K CPU @ 4.00GHz (8 threads) - 31.93 GiB memory`

> Interestingly I was able to reproduce the issue in any form from your steps to reproduce, but not by using your MRP, only a fresh project or a long term project of mine has this issue. This issue is preventing me from working on my project on that area, I'm going to have to wait until it is addressed hopefully soon. > > `Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Single-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4790K CPU @ 4.00GHz (8 threads) - 31.93 GiB memory` This is crazy. Mysterious. Thanks for the repro and thus giving me a sanity check. It felt weird to have to assume I was the only one being affected. That my MRP works on your end is so weird. And yeah, same here. I hope to be able to use 4.6 soon because the new Glow and SSR look fantastic. But not being able to properly use Themes I need to stay on 4.5 in the meantime (not a huge deal for me since I am still learning Godot anyways. But still, when working on content I would rather like to already be in 4.6) I meanwhile started Godot by console exe since someone mentioned it, and I get these erros at start of the MRP: And then this message when trying to edit the Theme (by clicking on it as described and filmed): Not exactly sure if/how related but thought to toss it in anyways. I do not have these errors when using 4.5.

Also can't reproduce, neither with the MRP nor fresh project.
Based on the above, it may be accessibility-related.

I've run into the same problem with the exact same error messages as HarDevSan. Both with a longer-term project, and a fresh empty project.

Launching godot with accessibility disabled no longer causes the errors and the theme editor can be opened normally, both from Inspector or from FileSystem, and a new Theme resource can be created normally.

```godot.exe --accessibility disabled <path-to-project>```

This might work as a workaround until the real problem can be found and fixed?

I can reproduce the issue. (And went on an adventure because of it. You can tell it was an adventure because I've added headers to this. Scroll to the end for conclusions hopefully useful for bug-fixing. I left the full story just in case someone more experienced spots a clue I missed.)

## Local Rust Installation Not At Fault (Probably)

Now, I do have Rust installed, so I checked the given directory, and confirmed that I don't have AccessKit installed as a crate there or in any project or other location. (It *does* appear that two browser extensions I have installed, one each in Firefox and Chrome, use AccessKit, but I doubt that's related.) I went ahead and checked to see if this bug still appeared when I had AccessKit in my `.cargo` directory from using it in a project. Because I ~~wasn't paying close attention~~ wanted to be thorough, I tested with `accesskit`, accesskit_consumer` (current 0.35), and `accesskit_consumer` (0.31.0, which Godot uses). No difference.

## Investigating AccessKit Source Briefly

Since I had it, I looked at the AccessKit source and found the error at line 136 in `tree.rs`. Note: that is no longer the location in the current build. Interestingly, it was moved to another line (with rather a lot of code between the old and new locations) in a commit that added support for multiple trees. I have no idea if that's relevant, but thought it worth mentioning in case Godot is trying to do something involving multiple trees.

## Investigating Godot Source

### Error Pattern Analysis

Finally, I followed a hunch on the count of times those errors appeared. The error from AccessKit said there are 10 nodes which are neither in the current tree nor a child of another node from the update. A quick count indicates that the Godot errors in `drivers/accesskit/accessibility_driver_accesskit.cpp` on lines 773, 788, 838, and 1319 occur 10 times each. Presumably there's a link.

(The "index out of bounds" errors appear 16 times for line 1047, 17 times for line 1065, and just twice for line 606. I assumed there wasn't an obvious link due to the lack of multiples of 10 present.)

For reference, `ae` seems to refer to an `AccessibilityElement`, and `other_ae` is another `AccessibilityElement` somehow being connected to the first.

773 is in `accessibility_update_add_child()`. Notably, `ae` is null while `other_ae` is fine here. So there's an attempt to add a valid child to a null parent in the AccessKit tree.

788 is in `accessibility_update_add_related_controls()`. Here, `other_ae` is null whereas `ae` is fine. I'm not sure of the argument meanings of `accesskit_node_push_controlled()` that they are handed off to.

838 is in `accessibility_update_add_related_labeled_by()`. Another case of `ae` being null while `other_ae` is fine. I'm not sure of the argument meanings of `accesskit_node_push_labelled_by()` that they are handed off to.

1319 is in `accessibility_update_set_flag()`. There actually isn't an `other_ae` here, just `ae` being null when flags are attempting to be set on it.

### Finding The Error Pattern In Source

I first guessed that the trouble started prior to `accessibility_update_add_child()`. That appears to be used solely when bound to `DisplayServer`. Notably, it gets called when `NOTIFICATION_ACCESSIBILITY_UPDATE` occurs in `node.cpp`. It passes a null check, so unless `DisplayServer::accessibility_update_set_name()` somehow modifies it (and if it does, then it looks like the issue would be in the AccessKit code), I would guess the issue isn't here.

It also gets called in `tab_container.cpp`, which I initially dismissed because of the earlier errors being about `SplitContainer`s, but then I spotted this starting at line 205:

```cpp
DisplayServer::get_singleton()->accessibility_update_add_related_controls(tab, panel);
DisplayServer::get_singleton()->accessibility_update_add_related_labeled_by(panel, tab);
DisplayServer::get_singleton()->accessibility_update_set_flag(panel, DisplayServer::AccessibilityFlags::FLAG_HIDDEN, tab_index != tab_cur);
DisplayServer::get_singleton()->accessibility_update_add_child(panel, child_node->get_accessibility_element());
```

That is the exact order in which the crash errors occur, for each of the 10 occurrences. Notably, the arguments clear up any confusion around `ae` and `other_ae`: it's always the `TabContainer`'s `tab_bar`'s tabs' `AccessibilityElement`s that are at fault. **So I have to assume the problem must be with several `TabContainer`s in the editor which are lacking `AccessibilityElement`s for their tabs.**

As an aside: thinking on what I already know as someone using Godot, there are at least 9 tab containers in Godot: the dock slots. Interestingly, the `master` branch has replaced `DockSlot` with `DockTabContainer`, so I wonder if that rewrite will happen to run into this bug somehow. Might be worth testing.

Continuing with the `tab_bar` line of thinking, within `NOTIFICATION_ACCESSIBILITY_UPDATE`, it appears to call `TabBar::get_tab_accessibility_element()`. Assuming `tab_bar` is not null, it asks it for the `AccessibilityElement` of each tab, starting with index 0. The method appears to simply request that element from each node in its list of tabs. That element being null is what triggers the errors shown. **So it's quite likely that this is fewer than 10 `TabContainer`s, but rather a total of 10 tabs lacking `AccessibilityElements`.**

**So assuming one cannot simply search the entire source to see what might be missing accessibility information, then a reasonable next step might be to compile a list of node types under each of the `TabContainer`s in the editor. Most notably, those related to any `TabContainers` within the theme editor ~~or the saving process~~.** (Probably the editor itself — check the final section.)

I'm afraid my lack of familiarity is stopping me here for now (that, and ~3.5 hours of debugging is tiring). I don't have any other potentially useful conclusions.

The `ThemeTypeEditor` over in `theme_editor_plugin.cpp` seems to have several places where `set_accessibility_name()` is called, but not everything has that. I'm not sure how much is needed to set up accessibility information. I'm not sure where the accessibility information for `Theme`s, or `Resource`s in general, are handled in the source.

### Final Follow-Up With `SplitContainer`

The bug is *possibly* unrelated? Unless it so happens that the null tabs also are or contain `SplitContainer`s, this is probably a separate issue. I could not find an existing other issue, however, which is slightly suspicious if people only have both bugs or neither.

## I Should Probably Look At The Theme Editor

3 hours in, and I decided to actually open up the theme editor, following the earlier suggestion of disabling accessibility for the editor. **It turns out that the theme editor has 7 tabs in the data type section, and 3 tabs in the default preview, for a total of 10 tabs.** Notably, all of these are lacking tooltips, which I feel would be rather useful, particular for the data type tabs. I checked the source and they are not given any by default, so I can't say if there's code elsewhere which is removing the accessibility data (which would've been a relatively simple fix, alas).

**Turning on accessibility and reloading the project causes the theme editor to crash on attempting to open the theme, so it isn't just saving that's an issue — it's specifically the theme editor itself.**

## Conclusions

### For Users

If you are getting this, go to your editor settings, go under Accessibility, and set Accessibility Support to `Disabled`. (You can also search the settings for "Accessibility" and it will appear.) It will prompt a restart. You can do this in the editor, or from the Project Manager by choosing Settings, then Edit All Settings, where you can see the editor settings. There is also a command line flag if you prefer that.

If you need a screen reader and this is affecting you, I'm afraid I couldn't find a workaround.

### For Contributors

The problem is almost certainly `TabContainer`s lacking `AccessibilityElement`s for their tabs, or those elements being somehow lost or overwritten.

We're almost certainly looking for a problem that consistently occurs 10 times. This could be 10 `TabContainers` with one child each, or a single `TabContainer` with 10 children, or any combination in the middle.

It is likely not an issue in the `TabContainer` class itself, but rather in something that extends `TabContainer` or that is a child of it in the editor.

It is reasonably likely to be a problem with the theme editor, as the crash occurs when attempting to open it, and it contains 2 `TabContainer`s with a total of 10 tabs between them. As a corollary, it is less likely to be the save dialogue that is at fault.

If it is not the theme editor, it may be worth compiling a list of nodes used as children of `TabContainer`s in the editor to investigate.

If none of the above works and the issue is not present in `master`, consider that the problem may have to do with the docks, which were recently updated.

I have no idea how this happens for some people but not for others — I would guess that it has to do with system accessibility setup while set to `Auto (When Screen Reader is Running)`.

Hopefully the above saves some time for someone else.

Just wanted to add the info that I had issues with drag resizing windows/tabs (SceneTree, Inspector or Output/Debugger) since 4.6.

Whenever I dragged on the edge of a window to resize it, regardless if hor or vert, the movement would stop after a bit of dragging when the 3D view was currently active/visible. I had to very slowly move the mouse, but still it was 'losing the drag'/feeling incosistent.

So I had to go to the 2D or Script view to be able to resize windows without this issue.

Turning off Accessibility in the Editor Settings completely fixed this also for me. I can freely drag resize any window again also with the 3D view currently active. My guess is that the mouse got "mixed up/confused" when it was on the edge of the 3D view. Felt like it "could not decide" which view/tab to handle.

Maybe it is interesting.
